references.text: The prophecy in Isaiah about light and glory that will come over Israel can be seen as a precursor to the description of 'anatolē ex hypsous' (the sunrise from on high) in Luke, which symbolizes salvation and God's intervention.

Micah prophesies about a ruler from Bethlehem, 'his origins are from ancient times, from days long ago'. This can be seen as a parallel to 'anatolē ex hypsous' in Luke, representing a new beginning and salvation.
Malachi speaks of 'the sun of righteousness with healing in its wings'. This can be connected to 'anatolē ex hypsous' in Luke as a metaphor for healing and salvation that comes from God.
